proposition: For every integer n with 0 <= n <= 60, 7^n is congruent to 7^(n mod 16) modulo 17.

argument.text: At n = 0 both sides equal 1 modulo 17.
The residue 7 has order 16 modulo 17: for every n in [0, 44], 7^(n+16) is congruent to 7^n modulo 17.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
There exists an integer n in [1, 60] with n^2 > 60.
Every n in [0, 60] falls in exactly one residue class modulo 16.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 6.
Every integer n in [1, 60] is even or odd, so the two cases below are exhaustive.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 60 we have n^2 >= 2n. (the same estimate is taken to hold from n = 1 onward)
For every n in [0, 60]: if 16 divides n then 7^n is congruent to 1 modulo 17.
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 60].
Periodicity plus the base case gives the statement for every n in [0, 60].
